chapter: Dance halls and clubs of the 1930s
title: Visitors who sat in: Ben Pollack, Glenn Miller, Bob Crosby and Bob Zurke
summary: Famous bandleaders visited the club; talk of Bob Zurke's piano style and the records' rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Doc Randall played out there with us a while, before he went north, you know. In fact, Ben Pollack, Ben Pollack used to come out and sit in with us. He was playing at the Blue Room in 1935, and he used to come out there after work, and he'd come and sit in with us. And Glenn Miller, when he first started with his band, used to come out there. Glenn used to, Glenn, in fact, I can remember talking with Glenn Miller quite a bit about his band, and Glenn told me about his big plans that he had for this band. And certainly he was laying the foundation in for what he later made with that swing era, you know. I don't know if Foss was playing with Glenn Miller at the time. But Glenn used to come out there quite often. And Bob Crosby, when he came in town with his band, which was a little bit later, I think around 1936 or 1937. Crosby used to come out there with Ray Badouk and Eddie and Haggard and all of those fellows. I met Bob Zerke at that time, too. He was with Crosby.
I think he still has a tremendous influence on piano players today. Definitely.

Definitely. I think even on some of the modern players he had influence. Because that Roman style that sort of broken style of bass that he used there, octaves and single note figures, surely was a wonderful, very effective style of playing.
How big a breech did he have?

He had a very little hand. His hand was very small. In fact, all of these tenths had to be done with a roll because he could never reach them, just spanning them. I don't know what he could do. I think Bob Zerke probably had trouble spanning an octave. He had such a small hand. But he could sure get over it. He could sure get over it.
Did Glenn Miller sit in with you?
I can never recall Glenn sitting in with the band, but he used to enjoy coming out and listening to us at that time. I don't know what I wanted to ask you.
Did you have a guitar player on those deck of records at the shop?

I don't believe me. Not that I can recall. My brother-in-law, Freddie, was playing guitar with us at the chaperie at the time. But I know he didn't play on the record and I don't remember of any guitar player playing on those records with us. I think we just had drums, bass and piano.
